# Data retention matrix

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:retention` from src/compliance/retention.ts. Do not edit by hand:
     tests/compliance/retention.test.ts fails when this file differs from the generator output. -->

This is the engineering record of what Lumi Noti stores, why, for how long and how it is removed
(spec 15 F237). Every period below is read from the code that enforces it. **It is not a privacy
policy and contains no legal conclusion.** Legal basis, controller or processor role, and any
regulatory retention period are to be decided by the operator. No formal security audit has been performed.

A test lists every table created by the migrations and fails if one is missing from the matrix, so a
new table cannot ship without a retention decision. It also checks that each removal mechanism named
below exists in the schema or the purge code.

## D1 stores

| Store | Data held | Purpose | Category | Personal data | Retention | Removed by | Exported in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

The workspace export lists each member name and email; the account export lists the full record. |
| `session` | Session token (a usable credential, AR-1), IP address, user agent, active workspace, timestamps. | Keeps a person signed in; the IP address and user agent help a person recognise a session. | `session_and_device` | direct | Until it expires (30 days), then removed at the next hourly pass | cron job `expired_auth_purge`; foreign-key cascade from `user`; account erasure (`DELETE /api/workspace/me`) | account. Metadata only (times, IP address, user agent). The token and the row id are never exported. |

Provider id and creation time only. The password hash and token columns are never exported. |

Short-lived security records; not exported. |

## Legal basis (to be completed by the operator)

Every row has a `legalBasis` and a `controllerRole` field in `src/compliance/retention.ts`, set to "to be decided by the operator".
This repository takes no position on them. The operator must decide, per row, why the data may be
processed and in which role, and record it with qualified advice before the documents are shown to
customers.

## Stores outside D1

Not machine-checked. The retention of these is set by Cloudflare or by account configuration, not by this code.

| Store | Holds | Retention | Enforced by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cloudflare D1 Time Travel | Point-in-time history of the whole database, including rows we have deleted. | Cloudflare-managed. docs/SECURITY.md records up to 30 days (read 2026-10-13); not re-verified for this document. | Cloudflare. We cannot shorten it, so a deletion is not erasure from this history until the window has passed. |
| Cloudflare Queues (deliveries and dead letters) | Queue messages carry ids and display text, never a credential (F173). | Cloudflare-managed. Spec 15 F237 records up to 14 days on the Paid plan; not re-verified for this document. | Cloudflare. |
| Workers logs | Redacted operational log lines: correlation id, counts, error categories. No payloads, URLs or tokens by design (src/platform/redact.ts). | Retention is a Cloudflare account setting that this repository does not configure: to be decided by the operator. | Cloudflare account configuration. |
| Cloudflare Email Sending | Verification, password-reset and invitation emails sent to a person (recipient address and the one-time link). | Cloudflare-managed delivery records: to be decided by the operator. | Cloudflare. |

## Deletion and its limits

- **Workspace deletion** is two-phase: integrations are disabled at once, and a cron purge removes every
  tenant row and the workspace after the grace period shown above (`src/pipeline/purge.ts`). Deleting an
  integration or source row destroys its wrapped data key, so sealed credentials cannot be opened afterwards.
- **Account erasure** (`DELETE /api/workspace/me`) deletes the person and everything that cascades from them.
  It refuses (409) while the person is the only admin of a workspace. See `docs/DSAR.md`.
- **Not erasure:** D1 Time Travel keeps point-in-time history for a period set by Cloudflare, so a deleted row
  can still exist in that history until the window passes (AR-6). Queues and logs are likewise Cloudflare-retained.
- Tables that carry an `organization_id` but are deliberately not removed by the workspace purge: `workspace_deletions`.

## Known gaps

- `invitation`: Expired or declined invitations are kept until the workspace or the inviting account is deleted.
- `legacy_orphaned_rows`: Nothing drops it. The operator reviews it after applying migration 0026 and runs DROP TABLE legacy_orphaned_rows (docs/RUNBOOK.md).
- `auth_users`: The tables stay in the forward-only migration chain. Whether a live database holds rows is unknown to this repository; the operator should check and drop them in a later migration (AR-10).
- `auth_orgs`: The tables stay in the forward-only migration chain. Whether a live database holds rows is unknown to this repository; the operator should check and drop them in a later migration (AR-10).
- `auth_memberships`: The tables stay in the forward-only migration chain. Whether a live database holds rows is unknown to this repository; the operator should check and drop them in a later migration (AR-10).
- `auth_tokens`: The tables stay in the forward-only migration chain. Whether a live database holds rows is unknown to this repository; the operator should check and drop them in a later migration (AR-10).
- `auth_invites`: The tables stay in the forward-only migration chain. Whether a live database holds rows is unknown to this repository; the operator should check and drop them in a later migration (AR-10).
- The expiry-based purge (`expired_auth_purge`) runs once an hour. `github_auth_states` has an index on its expiry (migration 0010);
  `session`, `verification` and `rate_limit` do not, so those scans read the whole table. Acceptable at current volume; add an index if they grow.
  A sanity guard aborts the pass, and logs `expired_purge_aborted`, if an expiry looks like seconds instead of milliseconds or more than half of a large `session` table would go.
- Accounts whose email was never verified are not purged by any job, and they cannot use `DELETE /api/workspace/me` (it needs a verified session). Only an operator can remove them (`RUNBOOK.md`, "Data-subject requests").
- Audit rows are append-only and keep the actor id, IP address and user agent after the actor is erased, until the audit retention.
- The workspace export does not include notification content (`notification_outbox`, `held_events`) or repository lists.

## Notes per store

- `user`: Accounts whose email was never verified are not purged by any job and cannot use the erasure route (it needs a verified session); they stay until an operator deletes them (gap).
- `session`: The session expires 30 days after its last refresh (refreshed at most daily).
- `verification`: Each record carries its own expiry (UNVERIFIED: the exact lifetimes are Better Auth defaults). Rows still valid at the time of an account deletion survive until they expire.
- `member`: A database trigger refuses to remove the last admin of a workspace outside a started purge.
- `invitation`: Erasing an account hands the pending invitations the person sent to another admin of the same workspace, so the invitee can still accept; sent invitations that are not pending (accepted, declined, expired) go with the cascade on the inviter. Invitations addressed TO the erased email address are deleted. A person whose email is not yet verified cannot use the erasure route (gap).
- `integrations` (integrations_credentials): Deleting the row destroys the wrapped data key, so a copy of the ciphertext (for example in a Time Travel restore) cannot be opened without that row.
- `deliveries`: Only terminal deliveries are purged; a dead-lettered row is kept until both its creation and its dead-lettering are older than the cutoff.
- `delivery_attempts`: Deleted with the delivery it belongs to; a delivery is only purged once none remain.
- `audit_events`: Erasing an account does not rewrite these rows: a database trigger refuses every UPDATE (migration 0008). They keep the opaque actor id, the IP address and the user agent until the audit retention above, which the operator must weigh against the erasure obligation.
